newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP sees flat performance after review.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP sees flat performance after review.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty (BHP) Co Ltd said on Monday trading conditions remained difficult and it expected a flat performance until it restructured and new projects were commissioned.

Announcing it had completed a review of its future strategies, BHP said there would be a number of abnormal adjustments to the full year to May 31 results, due on June 28, and that some of them would have an adverse impact.
BHP said after the completion of its strategic review it had re-affirmed its commitment to "superior performance and growth as measured against the performance of relevant peer group companies."

BHP Managing Director John Prescott said in a statement there would be an increased focus on return on shareholder funds and the performance of BHP's asset base, particularly those that were underperforming.
"As a result of this review, there will be a number of abnormal adjustments and these adjustments will be clarified in the release of BHP's full year result on 28 June," he said.
Prescott, in commenting on the fourth quarter results, said there would be some one-off items that would impact adversely on the results and trading conditions remained difficult.

"Given the assumptions regarding commodity prices it was expected that this situation would extend into next year with flat performance until the restructure takes greater effect and new projects are commissioned to contribute to earnings growth," BHP said.
Prescott said BHP's new projects woud provide a solid base for strong performance improvement over the medium term.
"BHP will continue with an aggressive growth strategy whilst at the same time seeking improved performance from its core assets to improve results," he said.
"The overall thrust of the Company is to concentrate on our best performing businesses and new projects that can perform at high levels," he said.
"We are committed to increasing our returns and to using our capital efficiently."
BHP's shares were down 17 cents at A$19.15 by 10.45 a.m. (0045 GMT) after earlier rising to a new year high A$19.42.

BHP's shares have surged 16 percent since it hit a 1997 low of A$16.45 on April 14, as investors revalued BHP on talk of a stronger world economy and after BHP announced a restructuring of its under-performing steel unit.
